title: What is known about 1RB1LE_1RC0RD_1LD0RE_0LA0LC_1LC1RF_---0RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LE_1RC0RD_1LD0RE_0LA0LC_1LC1RF_---0RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

This machine is 1RB0RC_1LC0RE_0LD0LB_1RA1LE_1LB1RF_---0RD with its states renamed (A here is D there, B is A, C is B, D is C) and so a different start state. Both runs settle into the same binary counter: digits written as 00 and 11, an overflow at the left end whose time doubles each time, and a marker on the right whose arrival at the end of its track restarts the counter in a new epoch. The twin's page has the full description.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps.

Where a halt would come from. The machine halts only in state F reading 0; F is entered only from E reading 1 and stepping right. In the first 108 steps F is entered 9,523,774 times and always reads a 1.
What a proof needs. The same as for the twin: a symbolic description of a counter increment and of the change from one epoch to the next. A proof for one machine should carry over to the other.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 181 cells have been visited and 103 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The same tapes as its twin 77 steps apart, except at the right end
claims.text: At each time state A is at the left end of the tape, the tape is that of 1RB0RC_1LC0RE_0LD0LB_1RA1LE_1LB1RF_---0RD at its corresponding event (state D at the left end) 77 steps later, except for the last two cells at the right end: at step 553,148,029 it ends …1 0 1 0 1, the twin's at step 553,148,106 ends …1 0 1 0 1^3.

claims.title: Overflows double, epochs
claims.text: At the left-end events the tape starts A>0 0 1^(2n+1), n growing by one per event and the gaps between events doubling; the counter restarts (a block 1 at the left end) at steps 8, 37, 206, 809, 3,782, 17,297, 22,706,588 and 81,579,887 in the first 108 steps. Read as digit strings, the events follow the twin's (marker walking right, restart when it reaches the right end; the restart's rewriting of the string is not understood for either machine).

claims.title: F always reads 1
claims.text: F is entered only from E reading 1 (1RF); in the first 108 steps it is entered 9,523,774 times and reads a 1 every time.

claims.title: A run-length frame map, every case proved
claims.text: At every head turn write the tape as two lists of runs (blocks of equal cells), left and right of the head: a frame with list parameters. A table of 68 cases, each a pattern on the first few runs of both sides (lengths exact or at least 4, the rest of each side any list), sends each frame to the frame of the next head turn; every case is proved for all values of its parameters and all lists by one symbolic run (RLCase.sound), so the frame map next = rlNext cases is sound (rlNext_sound). Between two head turns this machine crosses only a few run boundaries, which is why a finite table covers a tape whose number of runs grows without bound.
claims.where: cases, lean/Cases.lean; the runs in lean/Pieces.lean; generated by py/frames.py lean with tools/py/bbtools/listframe.py; library tools/lean/TM/ListFrame.lean

claims.title: The frame map from blank tape
claims.text: The run from blank tape reaches the first frame (init_f0, kernel), and the frame map is defined for its first 100,000 frames (native_decide). If it is defined forever along this orbit, the machine never halts (no_halt_of_total).

claims.title: The case table covers the run
claims.text: Every frame at a head turn in the first 3·10<sup>6</sup> steps (999,952 head turns) is matched by a case, and the case's next frame is the machine's (no mismatch, no unmatched frame); 68 cases at 10<sup>6</sup> steps, the same at 3·10<sup>6</sup>.

claims.title: No finite frame map with scalar parameters
claims.text: The frame-map method (stop at head turns, match the tape against finitely many templates with block-length parameters, fit affine cases) needs the tapes at head turns to fall into a bounded number of shapes. Here they do not: tokenizing the tape at every 7th head turn into maximal powers of words of length at most 4, the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps give 455,393 distinct shapes (exponents of 3 and more merged), 410,066 of them new in the last decade, and up to 36 tokens per tape; the number grows tenfold per decade of steps. For comparison the same count saturates at 32 shapes of at most 5 tokens for 1RB1LC_1LC1RD_1LA0LB_0RB1RE_1RF0RA_---0RC and at 89 for 1RB1RF_1LC1LF_0RE1LD_0LB1LD_---1RC_1RA0RD, where frame maps were proved. The cause is the counter itself: its digits form an arbitrary word, and the word of higher digits on the right grows too, so a frame needs a list parameter; the run-length frames above are such frames.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.155). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known; open, as for its twin (a separate question: the two runs share no configuration in 10^7 steps).

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RC_1LC0RE_0LD0LB_1RA1LE_1LB1RF_---0RD up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine is a renamed copy of another holdout, and like it runs a binary counter whose every overflow takes twice as long as the last. This page runs the real machine in your browser and lists what is known.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Same table as 1RB0RC_1LC0RE_0LD0LB_1RA1LE_1LB1RF_---0RD up to renaming the states.
Each overflow at the left end comes twice as many steps after the last.

sections.heading: A renamed twin
html: Rename this machine's states A, B, C, D as D, A, B, C and you get the table of 1RB0RC_1LC0RE_0LD0LB_1RA1LE_1LB1RF_---0RD, another holdout; only the start state differs. The two runs fall into step: whenever this machine is at the left end in state A, its tape is the twin's tape 77 steps later (when the twin is at the left end in its state D), apart from the last couple of cells on the right.

So the description is the same: a binary counter written in pairs of cells 00 and 11, an overflow that adds two cells to a solid block at the left end (A>0 0 1^(2n+1) becomes A>0 0 1^(2n+3)) and takes twice as long each time, and a marker that moves right by one 10 per overflow; when it reaches the end of its run of 10s the counter restarts in a new epoch (at steps 22,706,588 and 81,579,887). The tape grows like the logarithm of the time.
The only halting transition is F reading a 0; F is entered only when E reads a 1 and steps right, and in 108 steps it always lands on a 1.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.155). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 181 cells (155 left of the start, 23 right), with a density of 1s of 0.569.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

family: binary counter with a walking marker, in epochs
summary: The twin of 1RB0RC_1LC0RE (same table with the states renamed, another start state): a binary counter whose overflows double in time, with a marker that ends each epoch.
